title: Finite subextensions of $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ form a directed poset

proof.text:
For two finite subextensions $E,F\subseteq\Qlb$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-compositum-degree-bound] with ambient field $\Qlb$, base field $k$, and its fields $K=F$, $M=E$. Its hypothesis $K/k$ finite is exactly the finiteness of $F/k$, so the compositum $EF$ is finite over $E$ and $[EF:E]\le[F:k]$. Since also $E/k$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] applied to $k\subseteq E\subseteq EF$ proves that $EF/k$ is finite and gives
$$[EF:k]=[EF:E]\,[E:k]\le[F:k]\,[E:k]=[E:k]\,[F:k].$$
The field $EF$ contains $E$ and $F$ by the defining property of the compositum. No separability, disjointness or completeness hypothesis is used.

proof.text:
Induct on $j$ to prove that $C_j=E_1\cdots E_j$ is finite over $k$, contains every $E_i$ for $i\le j$, and has $[C_j:k]\le\prod_{i=1}^j[E_i:k]$. For $j=0$, $C_0=k$, whose basis over itself is $\{1\}$, so its degree and the empty product are both $1$. If the assertion holds for $j$, the binary result in step 1 makes $C_{j+1}=C_jE_{j+1}$ finite, containing all the required fields, and gives
$$[C_{j+1}:k]\le[C_j:k][E_{j+1}:k]\le\left(\prod_{i=1}^j[E_i:k]\right)[E_{j+1}:k].$$
This recursively defined $C_{j+1}$ is the compositum of all $j+1$ fields: any subfield containing them contains $C_j$ by induction and hence contains $C_jE_{j+1}$. This proves the finite-family assertion including the empty case. Inclusion is a partial order by the ordinary subset laws; $k$ is one finite subextension, and step 1 supplies the common upper bound $EF$ for any pair. Thus this poset is nonempty and directed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-algebraic-closure], every $x\in\Qlb$ is algebraic over $k$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension] to the one-element list $(x)$ gives the finite subextension $k(x)\subseteq\Qlb$, which contains $x$ by the definition of the generated subfield. For a finite subset $S=\{x_1,\dots,x_r\}\subseteq\Qlb$, step 2 applied to $k(x_1),\dots,k(x_r)$ produces a finite compositum containing every $x_i$, hence containing $S$. If $S$ is empty, use $k$. All fields are subfields of the same chosen $\Qlb$, so this is a compositum inside the specified ambient field.

proof.text: Every finite subextension is a subset of $\Qlb$, so their union is contained in $\Qlb$. Conversely, for $x\in\Qlb$, step 3 applied to $\{x\}$ puts $x$ in a finite subextension, hence in that union. The two inclusions prove $\Qlb=\bigcup_{E/k\text{ finite},\ E\subseteq\Qlb}E$.
